title: Clips on the timeline show pictures of what is in them
goal: On a five minute recording the clip is one long coloured bar, so the only way to find a moment is to play or scrub. The user chose: at Fit the clips stay the coloured bars the mock draws, and once zoomed in far enough for a frame to be recognisable, small pictures of what is in the clip fade in along it.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Picture: docs/design/video-vs-premiere/five-minutes-at-fit.jpg. Mock video.html (timeline section) draws clips as gradient bars with no pictures, so this departs from the mock and needs the user s yes before building.
acceptance: At Fit, clips look as they do today: the mock's coloured bars
Zoomed in far enough that a frame is recognisable, a video clip shows frames from its own recording along its length, fading in rather than popping
A picked clip still reads as picked, and its name stays legible over the pictures
Zooming and scrolling a five minute recording with pictures showing keeps every main thread pass under 50 ms
A walk at Next defaults on a five minute recording photographs Fit (no pictures) and a close zoom (pictures)
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on, and an audit written under queue/audits/ gives the try steps and a real picture
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: waiting on the user: pictures on clips departs from the mock's plain bars
decision "Should clips on the timeline show small pictures of what is in them?" resolved: Pictures only when zoomed in
triage 2026-09-26: goal and acceptance rewritten to the answer the user picked on the card (b, pictures only when zoomed in); the 'if yes' items are gone.

Adversarial review before building: (1) a first-time user zooms in with = or the zoom steps and sees frames appear; nothing to learn, which is the point. (2) Premiere/FCP editors expect frames along the whole clip at any zoom; the user chose bars at Fit, so pictures appear from the first zoom step. (3) Risks: decoding frames on scroll could stall the main thread or starve the playhead picture of decode time; pictures could hide the clip colour and name. Plan: pure layout/threshold in PhotonzCore (ClipFilmstrip, TDD), tiles anchored to the clip on a power-of-two time ladder so panning reuses frames and a pinch does not re-decode every tile, small separate decode lanes off the main actor, a bounded LRU of small frames, the clip's colour kept as a band along the top and the name in a dark pill over the pictures. Mock video.html draws no pictures; the departure is the user's answer (b) on the card.

Built: ClipFilmstrip (PhotonzCore, 16 tests written first) decides when pictures show (never at Fit; full from 1.5x once a tile stands for 8s or less, fading out by 16s) and lays tiles on a doubling ladder anchored to the piece. ClipFilmstripView.swift reads them on 2 picture lanes of MovieDecoder kept apart from the playhead's lanes, LIFO, 4 in flight, a read nobody waits for is never started, 400-picture LRU. ClipPiecesBar draws the strip over the colour with a 3pt band kept and the name in a dark pill. New walk step expectClipPictures and action timelinePanAlong. Also fixed Scripts/test.sh's video kit check, broken by e37a8618 (VideoKit.FieldRow called the app's PanelFieldRow): the gallery now supplies a stand-in, as it does for kitHover.

Review after building: zoom steps 18 to 33ms and scrolls 15 to 28ms longest pass with pictures, 41 pictures read within the wait; picked ring reads over the pictures; at Fit none. Side by side with video.html timeline: matches at Fit; zoomed, the gradient is under the pictures except a 3pt band, name in a pill (the approved departure). Seek freeze (pre-existing, 493ms with pictures off) filed as jumping-the-playhead-far-along-a-zoomed-in-long. Left rough, not filed: (1) the card's mitigation, hovering at Fit shows the frame under the pointer, is not built; it is an idea, not a defect, and it is in the audit's rough list for the user to react to. (2) pictures are small in the 28pt compact lane; asked as an evaluate question in the audit. (3) picking the clip costs about 60ms from the panel rebuild (755 Captions section bodies), not the bar; seen once.

Zoomed in past Fit, video clips show frames of their recording along them (fading in, 3pt colour band kept, name in a dark pill, picked ring unchanged); at Fit the mock's bar. Core ClipFilmstrip (tested), ClipFilmstripView + picture lanes in MovieDecoder, ClipPiecesBar. Verified by clip-pictures-when-zoomed-in-walk at Next defaults on a 5 minute talk: Fit none, 2x and 16x pictures all read, zoom/scroll passes 15-33ms, 6 real captures; audit queue/audits/2026-09-27-clip-pictures-when-zoomed-in.json. Test suite green (10018). Commit b7275bbb. Pre-existing first-jump stall filed as jumping-the-playhead-far-along-a-zoomed-in-long.
